title: Keep the Girls Apart (short)
style: warm and upbeat, speaking at a lively pace, no laughing

lines: Five boys and three girls line up at random.
What's the chance that no two girls stand together?
Five boys and three girls stand in a random order.
What is the probability that no two girls stand next to each other?
Line up the five boys first. That makes six gaps, counting both ends.
Two girls in one gap would touch. So each gap holds at most one girl.
Pick three of the six gaps. That's twenty ways, out of fifty-six equally likely sets of spots.
Twenty over fifty-six is five over fourteen!
Miss the end gaps, and you fall into the trap!
Why fifty-six? The full lesson shows two ways to count, plus every trap.
